settings.title: Settings
settings.ui_scale_auto_tooltip: Same text and button size on every screen: 100% (4K @ 150%, 2560x1600 @ 150%, Full HD…) because the Windows/macOS/Linux display scale already adapts to the screen. It only changes when they disagree: it grows when the display scale is too low for the resolution (4K @ 100% ≈ 150%) and shrinks just enough when the screen is too small for the window. All windows follow the scale.
settings.self_checks: Run automatic diagnostic checks (incl. backup integrity)
settings.self_checks_tooltip: Periodically runs internal diagnostic checks and opens every backup to confirm it is still readable and complete. This helps spot regressions and damaged archives before they are needed, but can be resource-intensive.
settings.self_checks_frequency_tooltip: How often to run diagnostic checks and backup verification (in days).
settings.ui_scale_quality_clamp: Ideal ≈{ideal}% → applied ≈{applied}% (readability limit for this resolution; remaining fit uses scrollbars).
settings.p2p_username_placeholder: Shown to whoever you send a save to
settings.p2p_username_tooltip: Shown to the other person when you send them a save directly — e.g. "Alice wants to send you save.zip". Leave blank to be identified only by machine ID.
settings.start_minimized_on_startup_tooltip: When SaveSync launches at startup, it goes straight to the tray instead of opening the window. Launching it yourself (double-click) always opens the window normally.
settings.minimize_to_tray: Don't close SaveSync when I click ✕
settings.hide_to_tray_on_game_launch: Hide to tray while a game is running
settings.hide_to_tray_on_game_launch_tooltip: When a game starts, SaveSync minimizes to the system tray and reappears when the game closes.
settings.show_overlay_on_unknown: Show notification for newly detected processes
settings.show_overlay_on_cloud: Show overlay when cloud saves available
settings.save_hints_desc: Extra keywords used to detect save folders, on top of the built-in defaults (one per line)
settings.save_correlation_tooltip: Also treats a file written at the very same moment as a known save path as a save. Finds save folders whose name has nothing to do with the game, but can pick up unrelated files.
settings.save_correlation_window_tooltip: Largest gap allowed between the two writes. Weaker candidates get 40% of it.
settings.min_kept_backups_tooltip: Minimum number of most recent backups to always keep, even if older than retention period. Set to 0 to disable.
settings.jump_tooltip: Jump to a section of the settings
settings.backup_on_exit_tooltip: Automatically create a full backup when a tracked game closes
settings.auto_scan_on_exit_tooltip: Enable live detection of save files during gameplay and confirmation of found paths on exit. Paths detected in real time are also used for automatic periodic backups.
settings.check_for_updates: Notify me when a new version is available
settings.check_for_updates_tooltip: About every twelve hours, check GitHub Releases for a newer SaveSync. You download it yourself — the onefile build cannot update in place.
settings.idle_after_minutes_tooltip: How long SaveSync must go unused before it does its heavier upkeep — releasing the loaded save and the decoded covers to give the memory back. Counted from the last input anywhere on the machine, or from the last time a SaveSync window was in use. Longer means putting it aside for a moment does not cost a reload when you come back; shorter means the memory is handed back sooner.
settings.auto_export_config_tooltip: Uploads the same encrypted config as a manual cloud export to your connected sync provider, so library and settings are not lost between machines.
settings.auto_export_config_interval_tooltip: How often the upload runs. It starts a few minutes after launch, only when a sync provider is connected, and skips if nothing changed.

settings.suppression_scan: skip path confirmation at game exit
settings.suppression_archive_skip: folder “{name}”: not added, not asked about again
settings.ignored_processes_hint: Processes for which you chose "don't show again". Identified by their full executable path to avoid blocking unrelated processes with the same name. Select and press "Unblock" to re-enable.
settings.excluded_paths_hint: Paths deleted during save confirmation (live tracking, auto-detect, general/extended scan). Restoring them lets a later scan find and propose them again.
settings.language_tooltip: Interface language. Applies immediately, no restart.
settings.ui_scale_tooltip: Manual multiplier (50%–150%). Only when automatic scale is off. Does not compensate Windows: 100% = design baseline. Preview applies on slider release or after typing the %.
settings.launch_on_startup_tooltip: Start SaveSync with the system, so games are watched from the first launch.
settings.minimize_to_tray_tooltip: Closing the window keeps SaveSync running in the tray instead of quitting.
settings.auto_sync_after_backup_tooltip: Upload every new backup to your cloud provider as soon as it is made.
settings.show_overlay_on_launch_tooltip: Show the in-game overlay when a tracked game starts.
settings.show_overlay_on_unknown_tooltip: Show a notification when an unknown process is detected.
settings.show_overlay_on_cloud_tooltip: Show the overlay when cloud saves are available for the game you just started.
settings.show_overlay_on_backup_tooltip: Show the overlay when a backup finishes.
settings.max_backups_tooltip: How many backups to keep per game. The oldest are deleted beyond this.
settings.backup_retention_tooltip: Backups older than this are deleted — unless they fall under the minimum kept.
settings.max_size_mb_tooltip: Save folders bigger than this are skipped instead of backed up.
settings.save_hints_tooltip: Folder names that mark a save location, one per line, case-insensitive. A fixed built-in set is always included even if you clear this box — anything you add here extends detection, but the built-in words can't be removed this way.
settings.backup_verify_tooltip: Opens each backup in the background and confirms it is still readable and complete, so a damaged one is found before you need it.
settings.backup_verify_interval_tooltip: How often the check runs. It starts a few minutes after launch, never while a game is being backed up.
settings.save_edit_copies_tooltip: How many copies of one save file the editor keeps before the oldest is dropped. A copy is taken every time you write to a save, so this is how far back an edit can be undone. Copies taken before a restore are counted on their own, with the same limit: 3 means up to 3 before edits plus 3 before restores.
settings.save_edit_copy_days_tooltip: Copies older than this are removed. The newest copy of each kind (before an edit, before a restore) is always kept, however old it is, so there is always something to undo with.
settings.p2p_max_per_game_tooltip: How many saves received via P2P for the same game are kept before the oldest is dropped — shared across everyone who sends you that game, not counted per sender.
settings.p2p_retention_days_tooltip: P2P-received saves older than this are removed. The newest one for each game is always kept, however old it is.
settings.p2p_files_dir_tooltip: Where files and folders that someone sends you by hand are downloaded: straight into this folder, laid out as they were sent, with no copy made afterwards. By default SaveSync's own folder. They are never added to your backups and SaveSync never deletes them.
settings.p2p_files_dir_pick: Choose the folder for received files
settings.p2p_port_tooltip: The port used to send and receive. Auto picks a free one each time. Set a fixed one (1024-65535) if you open it on your router yourself, or your firewall lets only one through. Applies from the next transfer.
settings.p2p_upnp_tooltip: Ask your router to open the port by itself (UPnP / NAT-PMP), which helps when you are behind a router. Turn it off if you forward the port by hand. Applies from the next transfer.
settings.p2p_friends_online: Check friends for tokens in the background
settings.p2p_friends_online_tooltip: Keeps SaveSync listening for tokens your friends send, so they arrive while you play. Turn it off and SaveSync only checks while the Friends panel or the Receive window is open. With a lock password, nothing is listened for while the list is locked (it is encrypted then): after a start it listens from the first time you open it.
settings.p2p_friends_media: Play pictures and videos from friends inside the chat
settings.p2p_friends_media_tooltip: Shows a received picture or plays a received video inside the chat when you press its button. This is the only place SaveSync reads a file somebody else made; turn it off to never do that.
settings.p2p_tls_tooltip: Sends files over TLS - authenticated, modern encryption - instead of BitTorrent's own (RC4). Nothing is copied. The transfer is TLS or it does not happen: there is no fallback to the other kind. It needs a port that can be reached (UPnP on, a forward, or a public address) and does not work behind the proxy.
settings.p2p_tls_note: TLS needs a reachable port on at least one of the two PCs (UPnP is on by default). With it off, this PC can still receive an offer sent over TLS, but only from a sender whose port can be reached.
settings.p2p_mode_direct_tip: This PC and your friend's connect straight to each other: the fastest way.
settings.p2p_mode_direct_note: Your PC connects straight to your friend's - the fastest way, at the line's speed. The DHT nodes that keep the mailboxes see your address as one more BitTorrent node - not who your friends are or what is said - and your friend sees it only while a transfer connects, not while you chat. To hide it, choose a proxy or Tor.
settings.p2p_tor_tooltip: Transfers and friends go through Tor (the program comes with SaveSync), so your friend, the relays and the DHT never see your address. Your friend has to use private mode too.
settings.p2p_tor_note: While this connection is chosen, neither your friend nor anyone watching the DHT sees your address, SaveSync accepts no incoming connections and it does not touch your router. The DHT is not used at all: messages reach a friend only while you are both online (they wait in your outbox until then), and a transfer needs private mode on at both ends. Transfers run at a few hundred kilobytes a second, and the first start takes up to a minute. Chat and new transfers follow a change at once; one already running finishes as it began.
settings.p2p_tor_missing: The Tor program is not part of this installation, so private mode cannot start. Nothing is sent.
settings.p2p_tor_failed: Tor could not start: {error}. It is tried again; nothing is sent meanwhile.
settings.p2p_tor_saved_note: Tor starts when it is first needed, once this is saved.
settings.p2p_friends_reset_tooltip: Forgot the lock password? The only way back in is to delete the friend list for good and start again. This works even while the list is locked.
settings.p2p_friends_lock_closed: Locked: it opens in the Friends panel, with its password.
settings.p2p_friends_lock_open: Open: it locks again by itself when unused (see above).
settings.p2p_proxy: Hide my address behind a SOCKS5 proxy
settings.p2p_proxy_tooltip: Sends every P2P connection - friends' messages and transfers - through the proxy below, so the other PC and the network see the proxy's address instead of yours. If the proxy is down or refuses, nothing is sent at all, never directly. Needs a proxy that does SOCKS5 with UDP (many VPN services offer one); Tor's does not.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_ok: The proxy answers, carries UDP and carried a name lookup.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_unreachable: Nothing answers at that address and port.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_timeout: The proxy did not answer in time.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_not_socks5: That is not a SOCKS5 proxy.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_no_udp: The proxy works but does not carry UDP, which P2P needs.
settings.p2p_proxy_test_no_dns: The proxy carries UDP but would not carry a name lookup (to a public DNS server, port 53). P2P cannot start behind it unless you let this PC's DNS do that lookup (the option above).
settings.p2p_proxy_test_dns_local: The proxy carries UDP but not a name lookup, so this PC's DNS will look up the DHT's starting server (it learns you use P2P).
settings.p2p_proxy_local_dns: If the proxy cannot look up names, let this PC's DNS do it
settings.p2p_proxy_local_dns_tooltip: Off (the default): behind a proxy that carries UDP but not a name lookup, P2P waits - nothing is looked up on this PC. On: only the name of the DHT's starting server is then looked up by this PC's own DNS, which tells that DNS server (and whoever watches it) that you use P2P. Nothing else.
settings.p2p_proxy_not_set: Fill in the proxy's address and port: until then P2P is paused.
settings.p2p_proxy_note: While this connection is chosen, SaveSync accepts no incoming connections and does not touch your router. It hides your address from your friends and from the DHT; the proxy's operator still sees that you use P2P. The DHT's starting servers are looked up through the proxy too (over its UDP), not by this PC's DNS. Chat and new transfers follow a change at once; one already running finishes as it began.
settings.p2p_proxy_login_not_saved: The proxy's login could not be saved safely on this PC, so it was not saved.
settings.p2p_friends_autolock_tooltip: How long the friend list may sit unused before it locks itself. It only locks if you set a lock password (in the Friends panel). Locked, the list is encrypted with that password and SaveSync stops listening for your friends: what they send waits for you. Never: only the Lock button and start-up lock it.
settings.backup_archives_too: Include archives in “back up everything” and “sync everything”
settings.backup_archives_too_tooltip: Archives are save folders you handed over without adding the game to the library. On, a sweep covers them like any game. Off, sweeps stay to the library and an archive is backed up by its own buttons or its scheduled re-check.

p2p.friends_reset_ask:
Delete the whole friend list?

This cannot be undone. From this PC it removes:
• your friend code (a new one is made when needed) and every friend
• all conversations, and messages still waiting to be sent
• the lock password
• anything being sent or received through friends, and the token waiting in the Receive panel
• what Settings remembers about friends (silenced messages)

Nobody on the list can reach you, or be reached, until you add each other again. Files you already received, link files you made and your other settings are not touched.

manual_path.description: Register save folders for backup by hand, even with no executable behind them. An absolute path, or one under your user folder, is taken literally; a relative path is looked for among known game locations.

When it starts at a user folder (Roaming, LocalLow…) that destination is already known on this machine and is used directly.

cheats.reason_es3_key: it is encrypted and its password is not in the game's files where Easy Save usually leaves it — put the key in an es3.key file beside the save and it will open
cheats.reason_alicesoft_asd: it carries no values that can be named — the gallery lists are a run of numbers with nothing saying what they unlock, and the engine scrambles some of the rest
cheats.reason_alicesoft_vsf: it is the flag file beside the save, and it carries no names to show a value under
cheats.reason_bakin_sgs: its values are written as a plain object stream with nothing naming or typing them
cheats.reason_tads_t3v: it is a TADS 3 VM state snapshot; the values inside are not named for editing — TAD-kit system.rec and JSON saves open normally
cheats.reason_unreal_key: the game encrypted it with a key of its own, and none was found — put the key in a {key_file} file beside the save
cheats.reason_unreal_key_add_game: the game encrypted it with a key of its own, and none was found — put the key in a {key_file} file beside the save, or add the game to the library
cheats.reason_artemis: its values sit in a tagged tree, and following one wrongly would write a number into the wrong place
cheats.reason_engine_encrypted: the engine encrypts it, and the key is inside the game's own program rather than in the save
cheats.reason_engine_encrypted_add_game: the engine encrypts it, and the key is inside the game's own program rather than in the save — add the game to the library so SaveSync has its executable to look in
cheats.reason_es3_in_game: it is encrypted, and the password is baked into the game's own build rather than kept in the save — add the game to the library and SaveSync will read it out of there, or put the key in an es3.key file beside the save

Some games, Ren'Py among them, also shift their autosaves along (auto-1 becomes auto-2), so the same name can hold a different save by now.

Reload it to see what it holds now (anything you typed and did not apply is dropped), or cancel to keep editing without saving.
